So, I just woke up to the news that my parents are separating and I would like to hear some stories, so I can handle this whole mess the best way possible.

Please share.
How did you handle your parents divorce and what are your advice?

I was pretty young when my parents got divorced, I was mad and sad, but as I grew up I came to understand their decision. Sometimes people are not meant to be together, and they can provide a better life for their kids being divorced. Well at least in my case. They were friends and understood that we (me and my brother) were in fact the priority, so if it's a tough divorced, try to keep them at least in touch. Bad divorces are also bad for children. Try that your parents stay friends for the sake of your education and well being, in case you're not an adult yet, or you still live with one of them. Try and understand why this is happening, and above all, help them. Support their decision if it is the correct one even if you don't want it to happen. If not, make them talk to each other and you.

My parents divorced when I was 12 and at the time it didn't make sense. I knew I'd be moving house and school which seemed horribly unfair but in retrospect it is definitely for the best. As hard as it seems you'll get over it and realise it's better them being separated than miserable, not just on them but also on you. Chin up, you'll get through it.

As a 12 year old, I said to my dad when he was moving out, "We're getting a kitty! I know you're allergic, but you'll be gone soon!"

Still feel bad about that one...
Oh my god. That is terrible. Have you at least apologized?
Lol I'm significantly older now. The chance has passed. Just remember to be kind to your parents, their trauma might be worse than yours (assuming you are a child in this family).
Unless your dad is dead then you can apologize. I learned that from apologizing to my dad recently about something I said as a boy. I'm 23 now, I was maybe 7 then.

I was 23 when my parents got divorced, they were very different people from when they first met and it was kind of expected (at least for me anyway, was a big surprise for my younger brother) a lot of arguments, big and small, not spending a great deal of time together except for when my brother and I were around.

I ended up being a shoulder to cry on for both parents and a go-between which made it a pretty stressful couple of years for all of us. I think they still speak now and then, but very rarely.

Both are happy with how life is now, I pray that is the case anyway...

I'm 25 and my parents are in the process of trying to figure out if they should divorce or work things out. I'm getting stories from both sides, and they are both fucked up. They both know I'm neutral and won't tell the other what they said, but its hard not to just smack them both and tell them why they are both screwing up.

Its weird being and adult and trying to find a balance between, I care about my parents and I'm an adult and haven't lived there in 7 years so its not my problem.
I'm currently going through this at age 24. Thanks for this. It helps.

Actually you have to focus on yourself and not on your parents. They are grown ups who lives their lives the best they can. They make decisions such as you are gonna make some at some points of your life (as you're not giving any hints about your age, maybe you have already taken pretty important one). The fact is they probably think that's best for them to split and you should just acknowledge the fact and take it as a given.

Hopefully it doesn't alter the love they have for you even if the impact on your practical relationship with them may change.

Plus the divorce is also a chance to discover who your parents really are. They'll have to reorganize their lives and they'll have a chance to modify the focus on their attention. They might get more involved in some activities or decide to do something they never had the chance to do during their married years.

I know it may sounds paradoxal but I think it may be easier for you to talk to them. If they're not screwed up, they'll also understand it's a rough time for you and they should give you the time and the explanations you deserve.

My advices are: 1) Don't take it personal. It's their lives and, even if you're a big part of it, it's what they think it's best suited for them right now. 2) Feel free to let them know if you're not comfortable about the new organization. They probably have an explanation for the choices they made and you could discuss that with them.

Well, I was 6. I cried a lot, at first. Then I realized my mom was much happier after my dad left. I saw this and decided that I can be happy with this too. I helped my mom around the house with whatever she needed help with. I lived with her for 2 years until she couldn't support myself and my two siblings by herself. So my brother and I moved in with my dad.

Now don't go thinking my dad was a scumbag for leaving. He wasn't, isn't. He was happier after the divorce as well. See my mother is a free spirit, Hippy type, and my dad is a strict, by the book police officer. They didn't click. They were in love physically, not emotionally. My dad still loved us and it broke his heart that we chose to live with our mom at first. Once we moved to his house however, we then really enjoyed it there. It was guy time there.

My advice: Try to see it from their perspective. If separating is going to let them be happier then it's for the best. I'd rather my parents be happy separate rather than despise their lives and stay together, you should want the same thing for them. Talk to them, listen and learn from them. I can personally say that my marriage is working great because I took what happened to my parents and learned that physical attractiveness isn't everything. I found a girl who was both beautiful and has a great character. It'll be hard for a bit but it'll be better in the long run.

If you need someone to talk to then send me a PM. I'll be more than happy to chat with you about it.

I was around 10/11 years old when my parents began their separation. I pretty much just kept it inside since there wasn't much trust between my parents and I already.

 

There's a lot to be said on the subject of what you could or should do, but the one thing I would tell my younger self then if I could travel back in time is be open and vocal about your situation. Just find people who will listen and get used to talking to them about it. The way I see it, the longer you spend holding your tongue, the harder it is to let go. For me, it got really bad because I never learned how to open up.

Of course, this is all easier said than done, but if you start listening to the excuses you come up with to justify not taking an opportunity to talk about what you're going through and really examining them, I think you'll realize like I did that they're just scare tactics to be ignored. Believe in the results, not your feelings - they're just there to serve as guide you when you're in the dark.

Hope this helps.

It really depends on how your parents handle it. It will be hard and the only thing I've found that makes it easier is time. If you're lucky, it will be a mutual breakup without much fighting and they will stay on good terms for your sake. If it's a rocky breakup then it might make it a lot harder.

I don't really have much advice as anything I could say would depend on your age and specific circumstance. What I will say is, don't pick one parent over the other. If you hear one parent badmouthing the other and it seems malicious (as in trying to make you dislike them instead of them just venting) let them know that you don't want them speaking like that. It's almost a cliché to say this, but it isn't your fault, your parents just weren't compatible and they will be happier this way. If you need someone to chat to you can PM me.

My parents are getting divorced?!

Seriously though, I'm sorry you're going through a hardship. I hope, at the very least, that it's actually a good thing for all your lives.

I was actually happy. I'd known for a long time, since I was fairly young, that my parents had a pretty dysfunctional relationship. I'm sorry you're dealing with this but honestly in the long run it's often a good thing - both of my parents ended up much happier as a result.

My parents are divorced and yet they still live with eachother. It really sucks because they fight a lot and it makes my brothers and I very depressed and then my parents fight over that which makes us even more depressed. It sucks, but I guess it makes you a stronger person.

I got the 'we're divorcing' speech when i was younger, but then they didn't divorce. They talked it out and decided to just stay together legally married just to take care of my sister and I. They slept in separate rooms and weren't always civil with one another but the midnight screaming fights finally stopped.

I remember being largely confused at the time mostly because they'd been having the screaming fights my entire life (like literally, my earliest memory was waking up in the middle of the night and hoping out of bed to ask them to stop so i could sleep), and thinking that i hadn't really realized that they weren't already divorced.

Later as a teenager my dad attempted to start seeing another woman and I thought he should have gone for it but my sister got very upset over it. To me it seemed natural for my parents to do what made them happy and not fighting, I never doubted that this would change how they felt about -me.- And it wouldn't change how I felt about them either. I would have been ok with them divorcing but I seriously appreciate their outside the box approach to the problem, it has taught me that there's always more options, and to focus on whats really important to me.

I haven't really asked them much about the choice, as a grownup, I might call my mom today and ask her about it.

My parents got divorced just before I was born. I watched my parents fight over custody of me for almost 10 years. Right up until my dad knocked up another chick and said chick didnt want me near her child.

Avoid if possible

Happened to me when I was about 11 or 12. After the initial emotional turmoil, I honestly didn't care. They were always arguing so it was for the best. The really sad thing is that my mum got together with somebody else and THEY ended up having the biggest fights/rows, probably worse than before.

My advice? Stay strong, don't take sides and definately don't hate one or the other (unless one or the other is an actual idiot...even then, try and not get involved)

I was 19 or so and in college. It was the whole "empty nest" thing. My parents had not been happy together for years and once I was gone there was nothing holding them together anymore.

At first I was mad.

The biggest thing is to not take sides. This can be hard to do, particularly if one side has done something like cheat.

I viewed myself like an airplane taking off from an aircraft carrier and the carrier sank. I was now on my own.
I don't remember how I handled it. All I know is I can't trust either of them when they talk about each other.

I just popped out, was just barely alive when everything took place. I dealt with it and still do to this day by offering my father anything he needs in terms of being in my life. My mother caught him with another woman, and this forced him out rather quickly, although she offered him a chance to stay and refused. At first I felt as if it were a reflection on whether anyone really "wanted" me around. This has been hard as I thought of this all throughout most of my childhood into very early teen years and further, but in all honesty, I look at it in terms of growing. I've grown to understand that everything will happen, and I can't, nor can anyone else, control what other people do or say. They will do and say as they please, and I need to just cope with that and not be so upset about garbage words when the truth couldn't be any farther away.

TL;DR: Parents divorced as I popped out, feelings of regret, feelings of self-hate, deal with it and understand you're not responsible for other people in this regard.

Hope this gives a bit of insight (although I didn't have all that much do deal with until I came to understand it).
